comparison: Perfect agreement with 100% claim overlap (C6-C13, C27, C30-C35, C124-C126). Both evaluations strongly support the core methodological advance and workflow integration. OpenEval describes it as 'a significant technical achievement' while peer reviewers call it 'a breakthrough' and 'cutting-edge methods.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement with 100% claim overlap (C47-C56) on transgenic mouse line development. Both evaluations support the characterization. OpenEval notes C56 as an inference with limitations but doesn't invalidate results. Peer reviewers accept the mouse line without challenge, noting only generalizability concerns for future applications. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement with 73% claim overlap (C36-C42, C44, C115-C117) on Fab-AuNP conjugate development. Both evaluations support the biochemical characterization and validation. OpenEval emphasizes structural evidence from cryo-EM, while peer reviewers highlight high specificity and resolution. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement with 89% claim overlap (C57-C74, excluding C63, C66, C82) on sample preparation protocol. Both evaluations support the methodology. OpenEval notes the protocol is 'well-documented' and builds on established methods. Peer reviewers describe it as 'detailed' and an 'outstanding guide,' acknowledging complexity as a practical observation rather than critique. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement with 100% claim overlap (C75-C79) on competition binding experiment. Both evaluations support the blocking experiment and its interpretation. OpenEval notes C79 is stated as expectation rather than quantitative measurement (minor limitation). Peer reviewers accept without question. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Moderate agreement with 50% claim overlap (C80-C88). OpenEval addresses cryo-FIB milling only, while peer result R6 covers both FIB milling and cryo-confocal imaging (C89-C95). Both evaluations support the methods. OpenEval notes strategic tissue orientation, peer reviewers highlight correlative targeting as strength. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Moderate agreement with 47% claim overlap (C89-C95). OpenEval addresses cryo-confocal imaging workflow only, while peer result R6 also covers FIB milling (C80-C88). Both evaluations support the correlative imaging approach. OpenEval notes quantification is 'somewhat vague' but appropriate. Peer reviewers emphasize fluorescence-guided targeting as strength. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Near-perfect agreement with 93% claim overlap (C96-C108). OpenEval includes C109 (ultrastructural features observation) while peer result excludes it. Both evaluations support cryo-ET data collection and reconstruction. OpenEval emphasizes CTF fitting and cryo-CLEM validation. Peer reviewers describe methods as enabling future research. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap (6%, only C109). OpenEval R8 focuses on tomogram observations including ultrastructural features and AuNP localization (C109-C111, C118). Peer R7 addresses data collection workflow. Both support their respective claims but address largely different aspects of the cryo-ET process. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Moderate agreement with 38% claim overlap (C110-C111, C118). OpenEval R8 also includes C109 (ultrastructural features). Both evaluations support AuNP localization at synapses. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with expected AMPAR localization. Peer reviewers affirm nanometer resolution and detailed structural organization. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Moderate agreement with 50% claim overlap (C119-C121, C123). OpenEval R9 also includes C122 (structural expectations). Both evaluations support quantitative AuNP positioning analysis. OpenEval emphasizes agreement between observed and expected distances as validation. Peer reviewers affirm nanometer resolution achievement. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement with 100% claim overlap (C131-C139) on acknowledged limitations. Both evaluations support the authors' transparent discussion of limitations. OpenEval notes these are 'honest assessments' that don't invalidate main results. Peer reviewers implicitly accept limitations as reasonable caveats, with Reviewer 2 echoing similar concerns. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial agreement with 14% claim overlap (C127 only). OpenEval R12 addresses C127-C142 (comparisons and future directions) and rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C127 lacks quantitative evidence and C128-C142 are speculative. Peer R9 addresses only C127 and rates as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 explicitly affirming the advancement over previous work. Disagreement on evaluation of C127.

Moderate agreement with 43% claim overlap (C128-C130). OpenEval R12 addresses C127-C142 and rates as UNCERTAIN, viewing C128-C142 as speculative future work rather than current results. Peer R10 addresses C128-C130 and rates as SUPPORTED, with reviewers affirming generalizability and future potential as reasonable extensions. Disagreement on whether future-oriented claims should be supported.

OpenEval R13 addresses established background knowledge (C1-C5, C14-C26, C28-C29, C43, C49-C50, C63, C82) supported by citations, rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These contextual claims were not separately evaluated by peer reviewers, likely considered uncontroversial background.
